issues.legal_issue: A finding that a jagir is proprietary does not by itself determine whether the jagirdar had subsisting rights to mines or mineral products.
material_facts: The competent authority classified the jagir as proprietary when determining compensation under the abolition law.
The classification rested on rights and interests in the soil and evidence about several incidents of the grant, but did not necessarily determine mineral rights.
The abolition law separately preserved mineral rights subsisting on the appointed date when granted or recognised by a contract, grant, law, custom or usage.
issues.conclusion: A further inquiry into subsisting mineral rights is competent after a jagir is classified as proprietary, unless the grant of mineral rights or their actual enjoyment in accordance with the grant was the basis of that classification.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(4)(i) and 2(xviii) of the Bombay Merged Territories and Areas (Jagirs Abolition) Act, 1953, classification as proprietary concerns entitlement to rights or interests in the soil and serves the compensation scheme under section 11; it does not necessarily decide mineral rights. Section 10 separately saves qualifying mineral rights. Accordingly, an inquiry under section 37(2) of the Bombay Land Revenue Code may determine whether such rights subsisted on the appointed date, unless the mineral grant or its enjoyment was the basis of the classification. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: proprietary_jagir_classification and mineral_rights_inquiry_sought and not mineral_rights_basis_for_classification

predicates.proprietary_jagir_classification: A competent authority classified a jagir as proprietary while determining the consequences of its abolition.
predicates.mineral_rights_inquiry_sought: A proceeding seeks to determine whether a former jagirdar had subsisting rights to mines or mineral products.
predicates.mineral_rights_basis_for_classification: The grant of mineral rights, or their actual enjoyment in accordance with the grant, formed the basis of the proprietary classification.

issues.definition: When a proceeding seeks to determine subsisting mineral rights after a proprietary classification, a further inquiry is competent if the classification was not based on the mineral grant or its enjoyment.

issues.legal_issue: A property-right inquiry cannot be initiated when the individual’s application merely seeks a record entry for a right already recognised and does not put forward a new claim against the State.
material_facts: An earlier order recognised the jagirdar’s rights to quarry gravel and stones in two villages, while stating that mica excavation rights were retained by the State.
A revenue entry recorded the gravel and stone rights in one village.
The jagirdar’s later applications relied on the earlier order and requested a corresponding entry for the other village; they did not assert the gravel and stone rights for the first time.

The inquiry concerned those same gravel and stone rights in the two villages, and the evidence considered during the proprietary classification had also referred to the jagirdar’s right to excavate and sell gravel and stones.
The jagirdar confined his claim to gravel and stones in those two villages.
issues.conclusion: The inquiry into those rights was incompetent because no claim had been laid to trigger the Collector’s power; the applications only sought entries reflecting rights already recognised.
issues.legal_principle: Section 37(2) of the Bombay Land Revenue Code permits an inquiry only when a property or property right is claimed by or on behalf of the State against an individual, or by an individual against the State. A request to record a right already recognised by the State is not such a claim. Under section 37(3), the Collector’s decision is subject to a civil suit within the prescribed period, so final adjudication of the rights rests with the civil court. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: claim_based_property_inquiry and no_new_property_claim_laid and applications_only_seek_entry_for_previously_recognized_right and inquiry_covers_that_same_right

predicates.claim_based_property_inquiry: A proceeding seeks an administrative inquiry into a claimed property right between the State and an individual.
predicates.no_new_property_claim_laid: Neither the State nor the individual puts forward a new claim to the property or right against the other.
predicates.applications_only_seek_entry_for_previou: The individual asks for a record entry reflecting a right that the State had already recognised.
predicates.inquiry_covers_that_same_right: The inquiry concerns the same right and property covered by the earlier recognition and the request for an entry.

issues.definition: An inquiry into a property right is incompetent when no new claim has been made and the individual’s applications only seek an entry for a previously recognised right that is the subject of the inquiry.
